일평 한국증시 신고가 및 상한가 종목 분석(26.10.20)  한눈에 보기  10월 20일 코스피는 215포인트(3.7%) 급락한 5552선, 코스닥은 27포인트(3.3%) 내린 782선에서 마감했다. 간밤 미국 증시에서 AI·반도체주가 급락한 데다 미국 물가 부담에 따른 긴축 우려가 겹치면서 외국인과 기관이 동반 순매도에 나섰고, 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스 등 반도체 대형주가 지수를 끌어내렸다. 장중 코스피 상승 종목이 93개, 하락 종목이 805개에 그칠 만큼 매도 압력이 시장 전반으로 번진 하루였다.  이런 장에서 신고가를 쓴 종목들은 세 갈래로 나뉜다. 첫째는 반도체에서 빠져나온 자금이 피신한 실적·배당 방어주(KT&G, 코웨이, 현대그린푸드), 둘째는 지수와 무관하게 개별 신사업 재료로 수급이 몰린 소형주(에스엠벡셀, HT로보틱스, 동국산업, S&K글로벌), 셋째는 특정 투자자의 지분 매집이 주가를 밀어올린 수급 이벤트 종목(지어소프트)이다.  상한가 종목은 재료가 더 뚜렷하다. 한국거래소가 시가총액 미달에 따른 상장폐지 후속 절차를 잠정 유예하면서 퇴출 공포에 눌려 있던 관리종목이 무더기로 튀어올랐고(형지엘리트·형지I&C·형지글로벌, KR모터스도 간접 수혜), 플리토는 3분기 실적 서프라이즈, KR모터스는 대규모 자산 매각 공시, 자이언트스텝과 에스팀은 AI·콘텐츠 테마와 극단적 저평가가 만나 가격제한폭까지 올랐다.  신고가 종목 분석  KT&G  KT&G는 지수가 3% 넘게 빠지는 날 19만3000원대에서 거래되며 신고가 영역을 지켰다. 지난 6월 21일 기록한 19만2400원이 넉 달간 저항으로 작용했는데, 15일 폭락장에서 5% 가까이 오르며 고점에 바짝 붙은 뒤 19일 장중 19만3800원까지 올라 돌파했고 이날도 고점 부근을 유지했다. 코스피가 급락할 때마다 KT&G가 오르는 패턴이 반복되고 있다는 점이 핵심이다.  배경은 실적과 주주환원이다. 한국투자증권은 3분기 연결 영업이익을 전년 대비 11% 늘어난 5150억원으로 추정했는데 이는 시장 컨센서스를 4% 웃도는 수치다. 수출과 해외법인 궐련이 역대 최대 분기 수량을 경신하며 성장을 이끌고 있고, 2조4000억원 규모의 해외 생산기반 투자가 마무리 단계에 들어서면서 투자 부담이 줄고 현금창출력이 부각되는 국면이다. 올해 중간배당은 주당 2000원으로 전년 1400원보다 43% 늘었고, 회사는 4분기에 배당 강화를 축으로 한 새 중장기 주주환원 정책을 내놓겠다고 예고한 상태다. 기존 2024~2027년 자사주 1조3000억원 매입·소각과 2조4000억원 배당 계획이 한 단계 더 상향될 것이라는 기대가 주가에 실려 있다.  밸류에이션은 PER 13~14배, 배당수익률 3.5% 안팎으로 시가총액 19조원대 필수소비재 가운데 가장 안정적인 축에 속한다. 반도체 비중을 줄인 기관과 외국인이 대안으로 고배당 방어주를 담는 흐름이 이어지는 한 수급 우위는 유지될 가능성이 높다. 다만 이날 상승률 자체는 소폭이어서 신고가의 의미는 급등보다 지수 대비 상대강도에 있다.  S&K글로벌  S&K글로벌은 지난달 28일 임시주총에서 S&K폴리텍에서 사명을 바꾼 코스닥 소형주로, 10월 초 기준 52주 최고가였던 2745원을 넘어서며 신고가를 썼다. 본업은 스마트폰과 디스플레이에 들어가는 충격흡수재·가스켓용 고밀도 폴리우레탄 폼 시트이며, 시가총액은 300억원대, PER은 8배 안팎에 불과한 초소형주다.  이날 별도의 신규 공시는 확인되지 않았고, 최근 재료가 누적된 결과로 읽힌다. 지난 9월 7일 전기차 배터리용 폴리우레탄 폼 제품이 세계 최대 중국계 글로벌 배터리 기업의 퀄 테스트를 통과했다고 밝힌 뒤 주가가 11% 급등한 바 있고, 해당 기업이 실제 적용을 검토 중이며 중국 전기차 업체와도 배터리용 폼을 공동 개발하고 있다는 내용이 성장 스토리의 뼈대다. 여기에 사명 변경 사유를 '기업가치 제고'로 명시하며 스마트폰 부품사에서 배터리 소재사로 체질 전환을 공식화한 점이 리레이팅 기대를 키웠다. 같은 날 유니테크노와 HT로보틱스 등 북미 ESS 부품주가 급등한 점도 배터리 소재 소형주 전반의 수급에 우호적으로 작용했을 가능성이 있다.  다만 최대주주 측 지분이 42%를 넘고 유통물량이 적어 소량의 매수로도 주가가 크게 흔들리는 구조다. 퀄 테스트 통과가 곧 수주를 의미하지는 않으며, 본업인 스마트폰 수요 둔화와 부채 부담이라는 기존 약점은 그대로다.  에스엠벡셀  SM그룹 제조 계열사 에스엠벡셀은 14일 상한가, 15일 15%대 급등, 19일 다시 상한가(4040원)에 이어 이날 4000원대에서 신고가를 경신했다. 닷새 만에 주가가 60% 넘게 뛰면서 거래소는 20일 하루 투자주의종목으로 지정하고 투자경고종목 지정 요건 충족 여부를 11월 2일까지 점검하겠다고 예고했다. 시가총액은 일주일 새 3000억원대에서 4700억원 안팎으로 불어났다.  촉매는 우주항공 배터리다. 회사는 14일 서울대학교가 주관하는 2900Wh급 저궤도 인공위성용 리튬이온 셀·팩 개발 국책과제에 공동연구기관으로 참여해 제조 기술을 확보했다고 밝혔다. 개발한 셀과 팩은 진공·진동·방사선 등 우주환경 시험을 통과했고, 방전심도 30% 조건에서 2500회 충·방전 후에도 초기 용량의 95% 이상을 유지했으며, 월 200개 수준의 셀 조립 생산기술도 갖췄다는 설명이다. 회사는 국내 위성 제조사를 상대로 배터리팩 공급 협력을 모색하며 민간 우주시장 진출을 추진하겠다고 했다. 19일과 20일 이틀간 국내 기관투자자 대상 NDR을 진행한 점도 매수세를 자극했다.  기존 사업 구조를 보면 자동차 부문은 현대차·기아에 워터펌프와 오일펌프를 공급하고, 배터리 부문은 1·2차전지와 ESS, 천무 무유도탄용 앰플전지 같은 방산 특수전지를 양산한다. 올해 들어 군용·배송용 드론 배터리팩, 8월 전고체 배터리 국책과제, 이번 위성 배터리까지 고부가 특수전지 재료가 연달아 나오면서 테마 수급이 집중됐다. 다만 EPS가 마이너스이고 PBR이 5배에 달해 실적이 뒷받침하는 상승은 아니며, 투자경고 지정 시 신용거래 제한과 거래정지 가능성이 생긴다는 점은 유의해야 한다.  코웨이  코웨이는 장 초반 11만1800원까지 올라 종전 고점 11만500원을 넘어서며 52주 신고가를 쓴 뒤 상승폭을 반납해 10만7000원대로 되밀렸다. 지수 급락 속에 차익실현이 나온 셈이지만, 10월 들어 10만원 선을 지지선으로 굳히며 계단식으로 고점을 높여온 흐름 자체는 유효하다. 2025년 7월 기록한 10년 내 최고가 11만4700원까지 남은 거리도 크지 않다.  실적 궤적이 상승의 근간이다. 지난해 매출 4조3100억원, 영업이익 7954억원으로 사상 최대를 기록한 데 이어 올해 1분기와 2분기 모두 분기 최대 실적을 갱신했고, 증권가는 올해 매출 5조원과 영업이익 1조원 돌파를 내다본다. 말레이시아에 이어 태국 법인이 40%대 성장으로 J커브 구간에 진입했고 인도네시아도 궤도에 올랐다는 평가다. 구독형 렌털 모델은 경기와 무관하게 현금흐름을 만들어내기 때문에 이날처럼 경기 우려가 커지는 날 방어주로 선택받는다. 주주환원 측면에서는 자사주 소각을 지속하고 총주주환원율을 20%에서 40%로 끌어올리겠다는 계획과 2027년 매출 7조원 목표의 밸류업 계획이 밸류에이션 재평가를 뒷받침한다.  목표주가 평균은 12만4000원대로 상단은 15만원까지 열려 있고, PER은 12배 안팎이다. 11월 10일 전후 3분기 실적 발표를 앞두고 선취매가 유입되는 구간으로 보이며, 이날 장중 되밀림은 지수 급락에 따른 기계적 매도 성격이 강해 추세 훼손으로 해석하기엔 이르다.  현대그린푸드  현대그린푸드는 52주 최고가였던 1만9950원을 넘어서며 신고가를 경신했다. 8월 2분기 실적 발표 이후 신고가 행진을 이어왔고 지수 급락일에도 매수가 유입됐다는 점에서 KT&G, 코웨이와 같은 방어주 수급의 수혜를 받았다.  실적은 단체급식 업종에서 가장 가파르다. 1분기 영업이익은 464억원으로 전년 대비 44% 늘어 컨센서스를 30% 가까이 웃돌았고, 2분기도 매출 5950억원(+8%), 영업이익 381억원(+23%), 순이익 306억원(+31%)으로 두 자릿수 성장을 이어갔다. 영업이익률은 6.4%로 0.8%포인트 개선됐다. 물가 상승으로 구내식당 이용이 늘면서 단체급식 식수와 신규 수주가 동시에 증가했고, 케어푸드 브랜드 그리팅을 본부 체제로 격상해 키우는 가운데 외식과 제조 부문도 고르게 성장했다. 제조원가와 물류비 효율화로 이익 증가율이 매출 증가율을 크게 앞서는 구조가 자리잡았다.  주주환원도 구체적이다. 발행주식의 2.35%에 해당하는 자사주 76만여주(약 133억원)를 11월 27일 소각할 예정이며, 2028년까지 매년 2% 수준의 자사주 매입·소각을 약속했다. 그럼에도 PER은 6배, PBR은 0.8배에 머물러 저PBR 밸류업 관점에서 여전히 싸다는 평가가 많고, 증권사 목표주가는 2만3000원에서 2만7000원까지 분포한다. 시가총액 6300억원 안팎의 중형주에 연기금 등 기관 매수가 꾸준히 들어오는 것도 특징이다. 멕시코 도스보카스 프로젝트 종료로 해외급식 매출이 줄어든 점은 약한 고리다.  동국산업  동국산업은 10월 8일 기록한 4890원을 넘어 다시 신고가를 썼다. 9월 22일 13.6%, 10월 2일 18.9%, 10월 8일 27% 급등 등 거래대금 수백억원을 동반한 급등이 반복되며 한 달 남짓 만에 주가가 두 배 가까이 올랐다. 이날 외국인과 기관은 소폭 순매도였으나 유출 규모가 크지 않아 개인 주도 수급이 신고가를 만들었다.  핵심 재료는 니켈도금강판이다. 2022년 사업 진출을 결정한 뒤 약 1300억원을 투자해 원통형 이차전지 케이스용 니켈도금강판 생산 기반을 구축했고, 9월 14일 생산 돌입을 공식화하며 2027년 북미향 46시리즈 양산 대응을 준비 중이라고 밝혔다. 전 세계적으로 니켈도금강판 업체가 5개 안팎에 불과한 과점 시장이고, 적용처가 전기차에서 UAM·드론, 로봇·피지컬AI로 넓어지고 있다는 점이 성장성의 근거다. 여기에 49.9% 지분을 보유한 동국S&C가 윈드타워와 해상풍력 하부구조물을 베스타스·지멘스가메사·GE 등에 납품하는 풍력 자회사여서 풍력 테마가 돌 때마다 동반 재평가를 받는다. 3월에 공시한 기업가치 제고 계획, 4% 안팎의 배당수익률, 0.5배 이하의 PBR도 저평가 논리를 뒷받침한다.  반면 실적은 아직 기대를 따라오지 못한다. 상반기 연결 매출은 3304억원으로 17% 줄었고 영업손실 54억원으로 적자 전환했다. 냉연특수강 매출의 80% 이상이 자동차 산업에 묶여 있어 완성차 업황에 민감하며, 신규 설비의 고객 인증과 실제 양산 시점이 확인되기 전까지는 기대 선반영 국면이라는 점을 염두에 둘 필요가 있다.  지어소프트  지어소프트는 52주 최고가 1만4340원을 넘어서며 신고가를 경신했다. 최근 3개월 상승률이 75%에 달하는데, 거래소가 이날 하루 소수계좌 거래집중 사유로 투자주의종목으로 지정한 점이 수급의 성격을 말해준다. 최근 3거래일간 상위 10개 계좌의 매수 관여율이 46%를 넘었고 최대 관여계좌가 외국인으로 분류됐다.  그 외국인은 미국계 투자사 미리캐피탈로 추정된다. 미리 스트래터직 이머징마켓츠 펀드는 8월 지분을 10.8%까지 늘린 데 이어 10월 6일부터 14일까지 1만1798원에서 1만4093원 사이에서 추가 매수해 지분율을 14.9%까지 높였다. 최대주주 김수철 대표 측 지분이 27.8%, 자사주가 21% 안팎인 구조에서 2대주주가 빠르게 지분을 쌓자 자사주 소각과 주주환원 압박이 커질 것이라는 기대가 주가에 붙었다. 회사도 8월부터 11월까지 100억원 규모 자사주를 매입 중이며 9월에는 자사주 소각을 결정해 5% 급등한 바 있다.  사업 측면의 재료는 자회사 오아시스다. 연결 매출의 95%를 차지하는 새벽배송 업체 오아시스가 토스 운영사 비바리퍼블리카를 대상으로 300억원 규모 제3자배정 유상증자를 결정했고 10월 8일 납입이 완료됐다. 조달 목적이 전략적 사업제휴에 따른 신규사업 추진으로 명시돼 토스 생태계와의 커머스 협업 기대가 오아시스 지분가치 재평가로 이어졌다. PER 10배 안팎, PBR 1배 전후로 과열 구간은 아니나, 특정 주체의 매집에 기대는 상승은 매집이 멈추는 순간 변동성이 커진다는 점이 리스크다.  HT로보틱스  옛 세아메카닉스인 HT로보틱스는 장중 20% 넘게 오른 1만1250원으로 52주 신고가를 쓰며 시가총액 2900억원대를 기록했다. 거래대금이 1400억원을 넘어 시총의 절반 가까이가 하루에 손바뀜됐다. 9월 중순 4670원이던 주가가 한 달 만에 2.4배가 됐고, 16일에도 거래대금 2700억원을 동반하며 신고가를 썼던 종목이다. 이날 새 공시는 없었고 최근 누적된 재료가 북미 ESS 테마 재점화와 맞물려 재부각됐다.  가장 큰 재료는 북미 AI 데이터센터 전력망용 ESS 엔드플레이트다. 15일 회사는 양산 1년 4개월 만에 누적 생산량 200만개를 돌파했다고 밝혔고, 대표가 미국 미시간 VMI 거점을 점검하며 주요 고객과 추가 물량 배정과 신규 프로젝트를 협의 중이라고 알렸다. 상반기 기준 수주잔고는 약 7000억원이며, 상반기 매출은 711억원으로 88% 늘었고 영업이익 37억원과 순이익 54억원으로 흑자 전환했다. 올해 매출 목표는 1500억원이다. 여기에 글로벌 대형 AI 데이터센터에 전력설비를 납품하는 국내 대기업의 공식 파트너로 등록돼 4분기 AIDC용 알루미늄 다이캐스팅 부품과 배전 어셈블리 첫 공급이 확정됐고, 3월 주총에서 AIDC 냉각·열관리 제조를 사업목적에 추가했다. 피지컬AI 홈로봇 부품까지 더해 ESS·AIDC·로봇 세 축을 내세우며, 10월 1일 산업부 월드클래스 플러스 선정 소식도 보탰다.  같은 날 유니테크노가 글로벌 배터리사의 북미향 ESS 버스바 하우징 공급사로 선정돼 상한가를 기록하면서 북미 ESS 부품 밸류체인 전반에 매수가 몰린 것이 직접적 트리거다. PER 35배로 업종 평균 57배보다 낮다는 점이 추가 매수 논리로 쓰이지만, 수주잔고의 매출 전환 속도와 공장 가동률이 숫자로 확인되기 전까지는 거래대금 폭증 자체가 과열 신호일 수 있다.  상한가 종목 분석  형지엘리트  형지엘리트는 5대 1 주식병합을 마치고 거래가 재개된 첫날 시가·고가·저가가 모두 1924원으로 찍힌 점상한가를 기록했다. 거래량은 107만주, 거래대금은 21억원에 불과해 매도 호가가 거의 비어 있었다. 9월 23일부터 10월 19일까지 매매가 정지된 사이 주변 환경이 급변했기 때문이다.  결정적 재료는 거래소의 상장폐지 절차 유예다. 서울남부지방법원이 10월 2일 주연테크와 케이엠제약이 낸 상장폐지 효력정지 가처분을 인용하자, 거래소는 본안 판결이 나올 때까지 시가총액 미달을 사유로 한 후속 상장폐지 절차를 진행하지 않기로 했다. 형지엘리트는 동전주 사유에 9월 3일 시총 미달 사유가 추가된 이중 관리종목이었는데, 퇴출 시계가 일단 멈춘 상태에서 거래가 재개되니 그동안 쌓인 공포가 한꺼번에 되돌려졌다. 병합으로 300원 안팎이던 주가가 1000원대로 올라 동전주 굴레를 벗은 점도 심리를 거들었다.  펀더멘털 쪽으로는 올해 역대 최대 매출 전망, 중국 합작법인 상해엘리트의 프리미엄 교복 사업, 중국 로봇기업과의 시니어 웨어러블 로봇 공동개발, 10대 데이터 기반 K뷰티 진출 같은 재료가 깔려 있다. 그러나 유예는 관리종목 해제가 아니며 본안에서 거래소가 이기면 절차는 재개된다. 상장 3사 모두 오너 일가 지분이 20% 안팎이고 소액주주 비중이 80%에 달해 변동성이 극단적으로 커질 수 있는 구조다.  형지I&C  형지I&C는 장 초반 25% 안팎 상승에 머물다 장 후반 매수세가 붙으며 상한가 1140원으로 마감했다. 형지 3사 가운데 가장 늦게 상한가에 도달했는데, 재무 상태가 가장 취약한 계열사라는 점이 반영된 결과다.  형지I&C는 8월 4일 코스닥 시가총액 200억원 미달로 관리종목에 지정돼 45거래일 연속 요건 충족이라는 시한에 쫓겨 왔다. 7월 말에는 이틀 연속 하한가로 1000원 선까지 밀리며 시총이 40억원대까지 쪼그라들었고, 유상증자로 시총을 방어하려 했지만 역부족이라는 평가가 지배적이었다. 과거 3대 1 무상감자 뒤 대규모 유상증자를 단행한 이력도 있다. 이런 종목에 거래소의 절차 유예와 형지엘리트의 거래 재개 상한가가 동시에 닿자 숏커버와 투기적 매수가 집중됐다.  사업적으로는 셔츠 브랜드 예작, 여성복 본과 캐리스노트를 보유하고 미국 아마존 입점, 중국 국영기관 네트워크 구축, 남북 경협 대비 TF 구성 등 재료를 꾸준히 내놓았지만 실적으로 이어지지 못했다. 상폐 유예는 시간을 벌어준 것이지 시총 요건이 사라진 것이 아니어서, 이번 급등이 요건 충족으로 연결되지 못하면 되돌림 폭도 그만큼 클 수 있다.  플리토  플리토는 오전 한때 8090원까지 밀렸다가 오후 들어 상한가 1만750원으로 직행했다. 거래량 93만주, 거래대금 93억원으로 시가총액 1700억원대 종목치고는 가벼운 거래로 가격제한폭에 도달했다. 장중 공시된 3분기 잠정실적이 방향을 바꿨다.  3분기 연결 매출은 178억원으로 전년 대비 51%, 직전 분기 대비 119% 늘었고, 영업이익은 90억원으로 전년 대비 217% 증가했다. 영업이익률이 50%에 달하는 분기로, 지난해 연간 매출의 절반에 가까운 매출을 한 분기에 올렸다. 이 숫자가 의미 있는 이유는 직전 악재 때문이다. 플리토는 AI 언어모델 연구개발용 데이터 공급계약의 발주금액이 4월 6억원에서 39억원으로, 이후 89억원으로 늘어날 때마다 상한가를 기록했는데, 10월 6일 계약금액을 89억원에서 40억원으로 정정 공시하면서 다음날 7% 넘게 급락했다. 계약 축소로 데이터 사업의 실체를 의심받던 차에 3분기 실적이 언어 데이터 납품 매출이 실제로 인식되고 마진도 높다는 점을 숫자로 보여준 셈이다.  52주 고점 2만200원과 저점 5510원 사이에서 변동성이 큰 종목이다. LLM 학습용 언어·음성 데이터 수요가 구조적으로 늘고 있다는 점은 긍정적이나, 수주가 프로젝트 단위로 들쭉날쭉하고 계약 정정이 반복됐다는 점에서 4분기 이후 실적의 지속성 확인이 필요하다.  에스팀  에스팀은 전일 2920원에서 상한가 3795원으로 마감했다. 거래대금은 36억원 수준이다. 3월 6일 코스닥에 상장한 모델·아티스트 매니지먼트 겸 패션 콘텐츠 기업으로, 공모가 8500원에 시초가 3만650원, 상장 첫날 3만4000원까지 치솟았다가 이튿날 하한가를 맞은 뒤 줄곧 미끄러져 공모가 대비 65% 아래, 고점 대비 93% 아래에서 바닥을 다져왔다. 10월 중순 시가총액은 250억원 안팎으로 PBR이 1배를 밑돌았다.  이날 뚜렷한 공시는 없었고, 시장은 글로벌 K패션 유통망 확대와 미디어 콘텐츠 사업 성장 기대를 상승 배경으로 꼽는다. 에스팀은 약 330명의 아티스트 IP를 보유하고 K패션과 K팝을 결합한 자체 IP 행사 캣워크 페스타를 운영하며, 유망 패션 브랜드에 투자하고 해외 진출을 돕는 브랜드 인큐베이팅을 신사업으로 키우고 있다. 지난해 매출 356억원에 영업이익 20억원을 낸 흑자 기업이 청산가치 아래로 떨어져 있었다는 점에서, 자이언트스텝과 덱스터 등 콘텐츠·VFX주가 급등한 날 저평가 콘텐츠 소형주로 묶여 바닥 매수가 유입된 것으로 보인다. 상장 당시 유통가능 물량이 30%에 그쳤던 가벼운 수급 구조도 소량의 매수로 상한가에 도달하는 데 일조했다.  신규상장주 전반이 보호예수 해제 물량과 실적 가시성에 따라 차별화되는 국면이어서, 이번 반등이 추세로 이어지려면 상장 후 두 번째 분기 실적에서 매출 성장과 원가율 관리가 동시에 확인돼야 한다.  자이언트스텝  자이언트스텝은 975원에서 상한가 1267원으로 마감했다. 거래량 98만주, 거래대금 12억원으로 극히 가벼운 거래였다. 며칠 전에도 786원에서 1021원으로 상한가를 기록한 뒤 조정을 받았다가 다시 가격제한폭까지 오른 것으로, 동전주 구간에서 벗어나려는 바닥권 수급이 두 번째 불기둥을 만들었다.  재료는 AI 영상 제작으로의 체질 전환이다. 회사는 자체 개발한 크리에이티브 프로덕션 운영체제 탭토를 전사 도입해 개인 감각에 의존하던 제작 방식을 시스템화하고, 사내 AI 에이전트 윌슨으로 생성물과 비용을 통제하며, 인력 효율화에도 제작 CAPA를 늘려 글로벌 랜드마크 스피어 프로젝트 같은 대형 수주를 소화하고 있다고 밝혀왔다. 현대차그룹 차세대 인포테인먼트 플레오스 커넥트에 실시간 3D 콘텐츠를 적용했고, 하이브아이엠과의 파트너십, 자체 버추얼 IP도 보유한다. 생성형 영상 AI가 확산될수록 실시간 렌더링과 고난도 VFX를 결합할 수 있는 회사가 재평가될 것이라는 논리가 바닥권 저가 매수와 만났다.  이날 열린 임시주총에서 사업목적 변경과 투자심의 강화를 담은 정관 변경, 독립이사와 감사 선임이 모두 가결된 점, 덱스터가 신작 투자 참여 발표로 장중 23% 급등하며 VFX 섹터가 동반 강세를 보인 점이 상한가의 직접적 배경으로 겹쳤다. 다만 1분기 매출 101억원에 영업손실 42억원으로 적자가 이어지고 있어 흑자 전환 숫자가 나오기 전까지는 실적보다 테마와 수급이 주가를 움직이는 종목이다.  KR모터스  KR모터스는 992원에서 상한가 1289원으로 마감했다. 19일 장 마감 후 나온 창원공장 매각 공시가 재료다. 경남 창원시 성산동 공장 토지와 건물을 강림중공업에 474억9000만원에 양도하기로 했는데, 이는 자산총액 942억원의 50%에 해당한다. 계약금 48억원을 받았고 잔금 427억원은 10월 30일 들어온다. 회사는 양도 목적을 재무구조 개선과 유동성 확보로 명시했고, 매각대금으로 창원부지를 담보로 한 전환사채 원리금 약 221억원과 금융기관 차입금을 상환해 금융비용을 줄이고 CB 오버행 부담도 털겠다고 밝혔다. 2023년부터 추진하던 부동산 처분의 상대방과 금액, 일정이 확정됐다는 점에서 시장은 이를 실질적 턴어라운드 신호로 받아들였다.  맥락을 넓히면 구조조정의 마지막 단계다. 9월 자동차 부품 자회사 다이나맥과 케이알트레이딩을 흡수합병해 다이나맥의 순자산 481억원이 본체 자본으로 흡수되면서 2014년 이후 이어진 결손금을 메우고 연내 이익잉여금 전환이 유력해졌다. 다이나맥은 국내 최대 냉간단조 설비로 브레이크 캘리퍼 피스톤과 전동화 부품을 만드는 연매출 800억원 규모 업체이며, 회사는 이를 발판으로 항공·로봇·고속철 부품으로 확장하겠다는 구상이다. 8월에는 2분기 영업흑자 전환으로 상한가를 기록했고, 22일 임시주총에서 사명을 다이나맥으로 바꾸고 본점을 대전으로 옮기는 안건을 처리한다. 시총 300억원 기준선을 밑돌아 관리종목에 묶여 있던 터라 거래소의 상폐 절차 유예 수혜도 함께 받았다.  지난해 매출 138억원에 영업손실 29억원, 부채 505억원의 이륜차 회사가 공장을 팔고 임차공장으로 옮기는 과정에서 생산 공백 없이 전환을 끝낼 수 있을지, 그리고 상장유지 요건을 자력으로 충족할 수 있을지가 남은 과제다.  형지글로벌  형지글로벌은 295원에서 상한가 383원으로 마감했다. 까스텔바작에서 사명을 바꾼 골프웨어 회사로, 형지 상장 3사 가운데 시가총액이 100억원 안팎으로 가장 작다. 8월 13일 시총 미달과 동전주 사유로 이중 관리종목에 지정됐고, 순손실이 자기자본의 49%에 달해 상장폐지 심사 기준 턱밑까지 몰렸다는 분석이 나왔던 종목이다. 결손금이 쌓인 형지에스콰이아를 떠안고 메자닌을 잇달아 발행한 것이 재무 부담을 키운 원인으로 지목됐다.  상한가의 직접 배경은 형지엘리트와 같다. 거래소의 상폐 후속 절차 유예로 퇴출 공포가 누그러진 상태에서 형지엘리트가 거래 재개 첫날 점상한가를 기록하자 계열사 전체로 매수가 번졌고, 시총이 가장 작은 형지글로벌이 가장 가볍게 움직였다. 올해 4월 아비트럼과 제휴한 스테이블코인 형지코인과 형지페이 추진으로 상한가를 기록했던 테마 이력, 강금실 전 장관 고문 영입 같은 화제성 재료도 투기적 수급을 부른다.  실적만 보면 바닥 탈출 조짐은 있다. 상반기 연결 매출은 316억원으로 69% 늘었고 영업이익은 9억원으로 491% 증가했는데, 형지에스콰이아 편입 효과에 더해 까스텔바작이 대리점 중심 유통에서 해외 바이어·아울렛·홈쇼핑으로 공급처를 넓힌 결과다. 그러나 동전주와 자본 훼손이라는 구조적 문제가 해소되지 않은 만큼 이번 상승은 펀더멘털보다 제도 이벤트에 기댄 반등으로 보는 것이 타당하다.  유의사항  이 글은 신고가와 상한가를 기록한 종목의 배경을 정리한 정보 제공 목적의 분석이며, 특정 종목에 대한 매수·매도 추천이 아니다. 본문에 언급된 수치는 공시와 보도를 바탕으로 작성 시점 기준으로 정리한 것이며 이후 변동될 수 있다. 특히 관리종목, 투자경고 지정 예고 종목, 거래대금이 적은 소형주는 변동성이 극단적으로 커질 수 있으므로 모든 투자 판단과 그에 따른 책임은 투자자 본인에게 있다.

신한은행 하나은행 해킹 고객 전원 VIP  신한은행과 하나은행이 해킹으로 정보가 유출된 고객 전원에게 VIP 혜택을 주기로 함. 실제 피해 여부와 상관없이 진행됨.  신한은 유출 고객 2만5000여 명 전원을 금융범죄 피해 보상 보험에 가입시킴. 1인당 연간 1000만 원 한도이며 보험료는 은행이 부담함.  수수료와 환율 우대 등 VIP 서비스를 제공하고 전담 창구와 직원도 배치함. 하나은행은 유출 고객 89명 전원의 등급을 VIP로 올리기로 함.  창구 송금·ATM·OTP 수수료 면제와 금융명의보호 서비스 가입을 지원함. 다만 정보 유출에 대한 직접적인 현금 보상은 포함되지 않음.  이번 조치는 2차 피해와 별개로 도의적 책임을 지겠다는 취지임. 반면 국민은행과 부산은행은 인과관계 검토 후 사후 배상 원칙을 고수함.  온라인투자연계금융에서는 최대 2만 원 현금이나 포인트 지급안이 나옴. 박준태 의원은 우대 혜택에 머무르지 말고 실질 보상을 해야 한다고 지적함.  정보 유출 자체에 대한 책임을 인정한 점은 긍정적이나, 고객이 체감할 수 있는 직접 보상이 빠졌다는 점이 아쉬움.

LLMjacking hits GCP: threat actors phish cloud admins, hijack billing accounts, and rack up hundreds of thousands in unauthorized Gemini API charges while keeping all AI workloads invisible to victim logs.  Key findings:  - Initial access came through Google Search ads bought against terms like "google cloud" and "gcp". Clicking the ad routed victims through a Google Sites redirect to a credential-harvesting page that captured both passwords and live MFA codes, then silently replayed them to GCP from 212.73.134[.]136. The attacker reauthenticated minutes later from a second IP geolocated inside the victim org's home country, a deliberate blend-in move to suppress location-based alerts.  - Once inside, the attacker enabled the Gemini API in existing low-usage projects, created service accounts with API keys, and assigned those accounts to roles/ml.admin and roles/mcp.toolUser. The organization-level IAM policy iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains was then deleted, lifting the domain restriction and letting external Gmail accounts be granted roles/billing.admin on the victim's billing account.  - The core technique was cross-tenant project linking: attacker-controlled GCP projects were attached directly to the victim's billing account. All Gemini API calls, prompts, and outputs executed in the foreign tenant. The victim's audit logs showed no prompt content, no model output, just a billing spike. Existing internal billing admins were simultaneously demoted to roles/billing.viewer, blocking them from detaching rogue projects via console.  - Within 24 to 48 hours of initial access, victim organizations saw unauthorized Gemini API charges reaching tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars. The attacker's phishing infrastructure spans a typosquatting network with wildcard subdomains: *.gprokl[.]com, *.gxoosl[.]com, *.gsoolg[.]com, *.gzoozl[.]com (note: no leading dot in source), *.groonl[.]com, *.gsool[.]space, *.gbrokl[.]space, *.gbrokl[.]xyz, *.gsoosl[.]xyz, *.gsool[.]xyz, *.gpoosl[.]com, *.groolg[.]com, *.gcslom[.]com, *.gcoalg[.]com, plus *.gboogl[.]com and *.groosl[.]com.  Practitioner takeaway: Hunt GCP Admin Activity and Cloud Billing audit logs for deletion of iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, grants of roles/billing.admin to external or Gmail accounts, unexpected linking of foreign GCP projects to billing, and service account creation paired with Gemini API enablement in dormant projects. In Google Workspace User Log Events, look for suspicious login flags and anomalous back-to-back reauthentication within minutes, which is the phishing kit replaying harvested credentials. Block the phishing IP 212.73.134[.]136 and the full domain list at your DNS and perimeter layer. The full IOC table is in the Wiz CIRT report.  #DFIR_Radar

Edimax BR-6478AC firmware v2.20 carries an authenticated OS command injection in the formWlanMP manufacturing-test handler, yielding immediate root execution from a single POST request. CVSS 3.1 score is 7.2 High (AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). No CVE has been assigned.  - The vulnerable handler is registered in bin/webs, an embedded GoAhead-style HTTP server running as uid=0(root) on TCP port 80, via websFormDefine("formWlanMP", ...) at binary offset 0x477a1c. The handler at 0x462a24 reads thirty radio calibration and EEPROM fields through websGetVar, then passes them raw into a single sprintf at 0x462fd0 using a format string of thirty unquoted %s conversions, and hands the result directly to system() at 0x46308c. There is zero validation between source and sink: no character filter, no length check beyond buffer capacity, no argument quoting, no switch to execve. system() forks /bin/sh with -c, so the entire shell grammar is available. A field value of ateFunc=$(id>/tmp/marker) executes the command substitution before shell program lookup, so even though rftest_old.sh is absent from the shipped image and the shell exits 127, the injected command has already run. That exit-127 fingerprint is itself a detection artifact.  - Authentication is required but weak. The route sits behind HTTP Basic authentication tied to a single /etc/boa/boa.passwd realm entry covering all /goform/ paths. There is no lower-privileged role: one realm, one password file, one account. The shipped firmware contains a pre-populated password file (CWE-798) using MD5-crypt, and the model's publicly documented factory credential is admin:1234. There is no rate limiting and no lockout on the Basic challenge, so the single-account realm is permanently exposed to dictionary pressure. The web server declares User root in etc/boa/boa.conf and performs no setuid, chroot, or capability drop. Root before the attack, root after, no escalation required.  - The scope of the problem extends well beyond this one handler. The report counted 91 /goform/form* handlers in the registration table, of which roughly 85 reach a system() or popen() call. A companion advisory covers a second independent command injection in the setWAN handler (POST /goform/setWAN, sprintf at 0x441ee8, system() at 0x441f1c), which uses a single-character semicolon filter that a pipe-and-hash payload defeats. The same setWAN implementation was matched instruction-for-instruction against a second Edimax firmware image, suggesting the defect lives in a shared software component.  - Detection is structurally poor. A POST to /goform/formWlanMP with thirty ATE fields is what the vendor's own management page sends, so the request shape is not anomalous. Anomalies to look for are: a non-factory user submitting a factory form, and shell metacharacters ($( backtick semicolon pipe newline) in any of the thirty numeric fields. The most reliable on-device indicator is a shell diagnostic reporting /bin/rftest_old.sh does not exist, the specific fingerprint of this payload reaching this sink. Post-exploitation indicators include unexpected outbound connections originating from the router and DNS resolver changes pushed via DHCP. Marker files written to /tmp are volatile and do not survive a reboot, so a reboot is an anti-forensic step. The vendor's own published materials indicate the BR-series legacy hardware is discontinued and will not receive firmware updates.  Practitioner action: if you are assessing this device, the binary SHA256 for the confirmed vulnerable image is ec39c0f9332361e37ab92f1999ac5f00f5742dd6db75f7cb26c0652cfedb32a1. Until replacement hardware is available, disable remote management, isolate the management interface to a dedicated VLAN, keep guest wireless clients off the management segment, and rotate away from the factory credential immediately. The full technical analysis and a reproducible proof-of-concept tool (Python 3, standard library only, loopback-restricted by default) are published unconditionally at the 0day Rubbish Research Team's site; the companion setWAN advisory and the broader disclosure archive are linked there.  #DFIR_Radar

Authenticated command injection in Edimax BR-6478AC firmware v2.20 delivers root command execution via a single POST to the WAN configuration handler, with no CVE assigned and no patch coming from a vendor that has publicly discontinued the product.  Technical breakdown:  - The flaw is CWE-78 in the setWAN handler (POST /goform/setWAN) inside bin/webs, a GoAhead-style embedded HTTP server running as uid=0(root) with no privilege drop. The binary is ELF 32-bit big-endian MIPS-I, 762904 bytes, SHA256 ec39c0f9332361e37ab92f1999ac5f00f5742dd6db75f7cb26c0652cfedb32a1. When wanMode is set to 2 (PPP), the pppUserName field from the request is copied into a stack buffer with strcpy, scanned by a single-byte loop that checks only for a semicolon (0x3b), then dropped unquoted into sprintf using the format string "echo %s > /tmp/UserName" and passed directly to system(). Pipe, ampersand, backtick, dollar sign with parentheses, and embedded newline are never inspected. The verified payload is a username of |id > /tmp/marker # which causes the shell to run id and suppress the intended redirect via the trailing comment character. The same injectable pattern exists on the PPTP (pptpUserName, wanMode 3) and L2TP (L2TPUserName, wanMode 6) branches of the same handler: a patch to the PPP path alone leaves two others open. A companion advisory covers a second independent injection in the formWlanMP manufacturing-test handler at POST /goform/formWlanMP, which carries no sanitiser at all across thirty fields.  - The sanitiser audit exposes how far the defense fell short. A hash-escaping loop does exist in this handler, at addresses 0x441f4c to 0x441fb0, but it runs after the system() call at 0x441f1c and operates on the configuration buffer handed to apmib_set, not the buffer handed to the shell. The developer escaped the stored value and left the executed value untouched. CVSS 3.1 score is 7.2 High (AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). Authentication required is High-privilege, one realm, one account, one password file, no lower-privileged role. The report also surfaces a second firmware image, BR-6208AC_V2_1.03, SHA256 3ad10a41d11c8cd59185eab6c9ce67b18cd2118942eb2201f48540d7846a0328, whose setWAN implementation is described as instruction-for-instruction identical, suggesting a shared source component across the vendor's router line, though that model was not tested and carries no score in this disclosure.  - The impact at root on this device is broad: all stored secrets are readable, including PPP/PPTP/L2TP ISP and VPN credentials, the administrator password file, wireless PSKs, per-station key material, and any certificate or key on the filesystem. The attacker controls the routing and firewall plane: NAT rules, DNS handed to LAN clients, DHCP, port forwards, wireless SSIDs, and the WAN uplink. Root can write the flash-backed configuration area and install a boot-time startup mechanism, so compromise survives reboots and can survive a partial configuration reset, requiring a full reflash for recovery. The shipped firewall script drops WAN-originated SYN, so the default network position for exploitation is a host on the wired LAN or an associated wireless client, including guests; remote management or a port forward moves it to the open internet.  - Detection is structurally difficult because the malicious POST is indistinguishable from a legitimate WAN settings submission. The report identifies two usable anomalies. First, a successful injection suppresses creation of /tmp/UserName: a WAN configuration POST that does not create that file when it should is the reliable on-device indicator. Second, the semicolon truncation means an injected payload stores a username the WAN link cannot authenticate with, producing a self-inflicted connectivity failure that doubles as a fingerprint. Fields worth logging on any surviving build are those containing a pipe, dollar sign, backtick, hash, or newline in the PPP, PPTP, or L2TP username parameters. /tmp is a tmpfs that does not survive a reboot, so rebooting is an available anti-forensic step.  Practitioner takeaway: No CVE has been assigned and the vendor's own public end-of-service notice states it will not develop new firmware for legacy BR-series hardware, so no patch exists and none is expected. Incident responders and network defenders should treat any BR-6478AC running firmware of this vintage as end-of-life hardware and plan replacement. Until then: change the factory credential (the firmware ships admin:1234 as a published default, documented as CWE-798 in the report), disable remote management and any port forward exposing the management interface, and isolate guest wireless clients from the management subnet, since a guest client holding the management credential is the most direct path to this handler. IOCs, the reproducible Python 3 proof-of-concept, and the full binary analysis are in the report at the 0day-rubbish[.]com URL above.  #DFIR_Radar

Unpatched OS command injection in TRENDnet TV-IP302PI firmware 1.02.38 gives an authenticated admin root shell via the NTP server field. CVSS 3.1 score 7.2 High, no CVE assigned yet.  Key details:  - The flaw (CWE-78) lives in the c64_Ntp_Server configuration parameter. The set callback at offset 0x2b668c applies a 48-byte length cap and nothing else: no character filtering, no address parsing. That stored value is later formatted unquoted into the command template "/hunt/msntp -ts %d -r %s &" and handed to system() via the GOT entry at 0xc274, which runs it through /bin/sh -c. A semicolon, backtick pair, or $(...) substitution in what should be a time-server address terminates the msntp invocation and starts an arbitrary command. The daemon runs uid=0(root) with no privilege drop anywhere in its boa configuration, so there is no privilege-escalation step: injection equals root.  - Two entry points write the same slot: HTTP POST to apply.cgi or SetTime.cgi (48-byte cap) and the ONVIF tds:SetNTP handler at offsets 0x286218-0x286264 (64-byte cap). A fix applied only to the HTTP path leaves the ONVIF path open, and the ONVIF cap is the more comfortable carrier for longer payloads. Both paths require valid administrator credentials through a fail-closed HTTP Digest gate, confirmed in the binary's own control flow: this is not CWE-306.  - Exploitation was verified in the vendor's own extracted root filesystem under qemu-arm-static emulation with a chroot, not against physical hardware. Three injection forms (semicolon, command substitution, backtick) each produced a root-owned marker file containing "uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)"; a benign control address 1.1.1.1 produced none. Because the payload is stored in a persisted configuration parameter, it re-executes every time the synchronisation path runs and survives a reboot. No daemon execution was observed directly.  - The daemon binary /hunt/hunt_server carries platform strings including PPPoE_TV-IP302PI and HuntDataDirect, identifying it as built on a Hunt Electronic OEM platform. Other camera models on the same platform may carry identical construction around c64_Ntp_Server. A companion CWE-798 factory credential weakness is disclosed separately; if compounded with a camera still holding its factory password, the conditional CVSS reading reaches 9.8 Critical, but that figure describes two defects together and should not be quoted as the score for this finding.  - Detection is hard because the write is operationally identical to a legitimate NTP configuration change: no failed login, no unusual response code, no privilege change. The usable signals are the value itself (audit the stored NTP address on every unit; any value containing shell metacharacters or simply not parsing as a hostname or address is the indicator), unexpected process children of the web daemon (anything other than msntp in that ancestry is anomalous), and outbound connections from the camera to hosts that are not time servers (the trailing ampersand backgrounds the injected command and pushes an attacker toward an outbound callback, which egress filtering will surface).  For responders: restrict camera egress to known time servers, audit the stored NTP field via the camera's own configuration API or management interface, and baseline the web daemon's process tree. If compromise is suspected, re-image and rotate every credential the unit holds: root-level access means both the filesystem and boot image were writable. TRENDnet was notified but delivery could not be confirmed; no CVE has been assigned and no fixed firmware is known to exist. The full technical analysis and a Python 3 proof of concept are in the 0day Rubbish report at 0day-rubbish[.]com/blog/trendnet-tv-ip302pi-ntp-command-injection-root-rce.  #DFIR_Radar

Incident response gets harder when service logs establish identity but not resource ownership.  For cross-project queue access, knowing which account connected is only half the picture. Investigators also need to know which project each operation targeted, especially if queues were inspected or removed.  In practical terms, it is a good time to: • Check whether Zaqar request records include principal, session, operation, and target project. • Correlate WebSocket connection records with queue mutations where available. • Preserve relevant application and proxy logs under current retention rules. • Test whether investigators can distinguish authorized administration from cross-tenant activity.  #SecurityOperations #IncidentResponse #OpenStack #ThreatDetection linuxsecurity.com/news/cloud…

Shelby County resident sues MLGW after utility worker fatally sh00ts dog on North Shelby lawn  A Shelby County homeowner has filed suit against Memphis Light, Gas and Water after a utility revenue protection employee sh0t and died the man’s dog on the front lawn of his North Shelby County residence on the morning of Thursday, Sept. 10. The suit was filed by attorney Kevin Snider on behalf of Bryan McGarah, who says his four-year-old dog was friendly and posed no threat to workers.  According to the complaint and statements from the utility, MLGW revenue protection workers had identified themselves and were on the property to inspect equipment when the dog ran out of the house and approached an employee. MLGW confirmed the worker assigned to its Revenue Protection Team was armed as part of his duties; the utility says the employee fired because he was charged by the dog. The Shelby County Sheriff’s Office conducted an investigation and determined the sh00ting was justified, the utility told reporters.  McGarah’s filing alleges violations of Tennessee’s “T-Bo Law,” which permits owners to seek specified damages when a companion animal is wrongfully died. The plaintiff disputes the utility’s account, describing the dog as nonaggressive and asserting the sh00ting was sudden. A Change.org petition seeking policy changes at MLGW has gathered signatures in response to the incident.  At this time the case is in civil litigation following the suit filing; the Sheriff’s Office investigative finding that the sh00ting was justified is part of the record cited by the utility. No criminal charges are reported in the available documentation.  All individuals accused of a crime are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

Kernel patch management has a blind spot when teams track installed packages but not the kernel that is actually running.  A fix can be present on disk while the host continues operating on the previous kernel until reboot. For an issue involving kernel behavior such as the perf filter path, that distinction is operationally decisive.  It also complicates incident response: package state, boot state, and vulnerability-scanner state can tell different stories.  The useful control is not simply “kernel package updated.” It is proof that the intended kernel is active.  In practical terms, it is a good time to: - compare uname-r with the newest approved installed kernel package - identify hosts awaiting reboot after kernel security updates - verify bootloader defaults point to the approved kernel - compare vulnerability-scanner results with the running kernel and distribution backport status  #PatchManagement #LinuxSecurity #SysAdmin #SecurityOperations linuxsecurity.com/news/secur…

Taxonomy Escalation Fatigue Prevention: Reducing Alert Noise Without Missing Critical Risk @RialoHQ   Escalation protects governance when monitoring detects serious problems.  But too many escalations can weaken the system.  Operators start ignoring repeated warnings. Reviewers spend time investigating harmless anomalies. Critical alerts get buried under routine notifications. A taxonomy escalation fatigue prevention framework reduces unnecessary alerts while ensuring high-risk signals still receive immediate attention. The principle is simple:  Reduce noise, not protection.  1. Why escalation fatigue matters  Alert fatigue happens when the volume of notifications exceeds the team's ability to respond effectively.  Common causes include:  duplicate alerts from multiple systems  thresholds that are too sensitive  repeated warnings for unresolved issues  low-risk findings routed as critical alerts without clear actions monitoring rules that never get reviewed The result is slower response and weaker decision protection. 2. Alert deduplication One underlying issue should not generate multiple independent escalations.  Example:  A certification failure triggers:  registry warning  dashboard alert  scorecard failure decision ledger notification Instead of four separate incidents, group them under one incident ID. Preserve all affected signals and dependencies, but assign one response owner. Deduplication should reduce repeated work without hiding the scope of the issue.  3. Smart suppression rules  Suppress alerts when:  the same unchanged issue is already being handled  a low-risk condition is within an approved maintenance window  an informational signal has no new evidence  a resolved issue is producing delayed duplicate notifications Never suppress: critical control failures approval bypasses  failed safe-exit controls  new risk exposure expired high-risk exceptions affecting active decisions Every suppression rule should have an owner, expiration, and audit trail. 4. Threshold tuning Escalation thresholds should reflect actual decision risk.  Examples:  SignalEscalation ruleMinor dashboard delayAlert after repeated failuresMissing low-risk evidenceNotify ownerRepeated stale evidenceEscalate to reviewerConfidence mismatch affecting approvalRestrict decisionCritical approval bypassImmediate incident  Thresholds should be reviewed against actual incidents.  If too many harmless alerts escalate, tighten the conditions. If serious issues are detected late, strengthen them. 5. Escalation ownership Every actionable alert should include: signal ID severity affected decision response owner required action response deadline escalation path Avoid sending alerts to large groups without assigning responsibility. Shared visibility is useful. Shared ambiguity is not. 6. Measure escalation quality  Track:  alert volume by severity  duplicate alert rate  false-positive rate  alerts without action  time to protective action repeated escalations for the same issue critical incidents detected late operator workload The most important balance is between unnecessary escalations and missed critical risk. Reducing alert volume means little if detection quality also declines. 7. Continuous tuning  Review escalation performance monthly.  Ask:  which alerts never lead to action?  which signals repeatedly escalate?  which thresholds are too sensitive?  which critical issues were detected late? which alerts can be grouped? which suppression rules are still justified? Change one group of rules at a time, then validate the results. Do not optimize alert volume at the expense of decision safety. 8. Common anti-patterns Suppressing everything noisy Critical failures disappear alongside harmless warnings.  Escalating everything immediately  Operators lose the ability to distinguish urgency.  No suppression expiration  Temporary silencing becomes permanent.  Counting fewer alerts as success  The dashboard improves while detection weakens. Ignoring operator feedback Alert rules remain disconnected from actual response work. 9. The real standard Effective escalation should be selective, reliable, and actionable. A mature governance system:  groups duplicate alerts  suppresses harmless repetition  protects critical triggers  tunes thresholds using real outcomes  assigns clear response ownership  measures missed risks as well as false positives  The goal is not fewer alerts at any cost.  It is fewer unnecessary interruptions and faster action when governance genuinely needs protection.  A healthy escalation system stays quiet when operations are safe and unmistakably clear when they are not.

Cornell Case - One Question, Two Very Different Accounts  Jane Doe sent a letter to Cornell's Faculty Senate explaining that a secondhand account of a conversation between the former Tri Delta president and Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff diminished her confidence in the administration's ability to take her allegations seriously.  According to Doe, the sorority president told her Kotlikoff had asked something along the lines of, "Why did she wait so long to report it?"  The sorority president reportedly interpreted that question as expressing doubt about Doe's allegations.  But there's a problem with that interpretation.  Cornell disputes that Kotlikoff was questioning Doe at all.  According to Cornell's official response, Kotlikoff was asking why bystanders who were aware of the allegations hadn't reported them through the university's anonymous tip line, particularly given the social media activity surrounding the incident.  Cornell Dean of Faculty Chris Schaffer said he obtained a contemporaneous account from another university official who attended the January 2025 meeting.  According to that account, Kotlikoff's question concerned the failure of bystanders to report the allegations,  not why Doe herself waited to come forward.  But even if Kotlikoff had asked why Doe waited approximately three weeks to report the alleged assault, would that automatically mean he doubted her?  I don't think so.  There are many reasons someone might delay reporting a sexual assault. Asking about that delay can be a legitimate part of understanding the circumstances and timeline.  A question isn't necessarily an accusation, and without the surrounding conversation, we shouldn't automatically assign it a motive.  But I think there's something more important to examine.  How seriously did Cornell actually investigate Doe's allegations?  Here's what public reporting tells us.  Cornell University Police investigation  Doe was interviewed over two days - November 14–15, 2024.  Her police interview generated approximately 120 pages of transcript.  A six-page sworn statement was prepared, reviewed, and signed by Doe.  The district attorney's office received that statement, although questions remain about the extent of the additional evidence it reviewed.  Cornell Title IX investigation and disciplinary proceedings  Approximately 50 interviews involving 32 witnesses.  CBS obtained 565 pages of Title IX interview transcripts.  The New York Times reviewed more than 1,000 pages of investigative records.  A university disciplinary hearing lasted 12 days.  The proceedings resulted in disciplinary findings and sanctions against several students.  That's just what has been leaked to the media, so there could be overlap, and there could be more.  Still, we're talking about an extensive investigation involving dozens of witnesses, hundreds of pages of testimony, and nearly two weeks of disciplinary hearings.  Does that mean Cornell handled every aspect of this case appropriately? Not necessarily.  I think it's reasonable to question the administration's decisions, just as it's reasonable to question whether criticism of those decisions is supported by the full record.  If we're going to evaluate Cornell's response, shouldn't we examine what the university actually did rather than judge its commitment to investigating the allegations based on a disputed, secondhand account of one question?

Chinese thinkers approach “what’s left for humans after AI” from a different starting point than Western debates, emphasizing the heart/mind (心, xīn), humaneness/benevolence (仁, rén), and relations between people rather than intelligence as the core of humanity.  Western anxiety often stems from defining humans as Homo sapiens (“wise man”), so advanced AI feels like a direct threat to what makes us human. Chinese traditions (drawing on Confucianism and Taoism) do not place intelligence at the center in the same way. They focus instead on the heart-mind—where feeling, judgment, right/wrong, and care for others reside—and on rén as the defining quality of being human.  Liu Yongmou (philosopher of technology at Renmin University): Humanity’s biggest problem is the “machinization of humans,” not the humanization of machines. This echoes the Zhuangzi story of a gardener who rejects a labor-saving device because using machines produces a “machine-heart” (jīxīn)—a calculating mind that loses simplicity.  Zhao Tingyang (Chinese Academy of Social Sciences): Trying to make AI share human values “may very well be a suicidal mistake.” Bad AI outcomes can be fought, but “humanity may die of all the good things AI creates.” Western debates tend to fear AI failure (rogue systems, job loss, weapons); the Chinese discussion is more wary of AI success and abundance eroding what matters.  The West often guards the boundary between humans and machines. In Chinese thinking, humanity lives in the space between people, so a machine with a heart takes nothing away from ours—what threatens it is a machine that leaves us without each other. Some Chinese figures (such as Zhu Songchun) seek to “set a heart for machines,” while others worry machines will fill the relational space.  On “uselessness”: Fears that AI will make people useless rest on the premise that a person’s worth equals their utility. A classic Taoist image of a tree that survives precisely because it is “useless” suggests that predicted uselessness might instead be a form of preservation or freedom.

⚠️ Alleged Habib Metropolitan Bank Data Leak Exposes Customer PII on Darkweb  A post on an underground forum claims to have obtained sensitive customer data from Habib Metropolitan Bank Limited (HMB), a major commercial bank in Pakistan. The listing, titled "HABIB METROPOLITAN BANK LTD DATA," displays sample records containing personally identifiable information (PII) and financial account details for numerous individuals.  The leaked dataset appears to include the following fields: *   Full names of account holders *   National Identity Card (CNIC) numbers *   Residential addresses *   Bank branch codes and names *   Account numbers and types *   Currency and balance information  Habib Metropolitan Bank is one of Pakistan's largest private-sector banks, serving millions of customers across the country. The exposure of CNIC numbers alongside bank account details poses a significant risk to affected individuals, potentially enabling identity theft, social engineering attacks, or targeted fraud. The data samples provided in the thread reference branches in Karachi, Lahore, and Sukkur, indicating a broad geographic scope within Pakistan.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Habib Metropolitan Bank or Pakistani cybersecurity authorities. The threat actor behind the post has not been identified in the source material, and no ransom demand was explicitly stated in the visible portion of the thread, though a Telegram contact was provided for further inquiries.  #DataBreach #HabibMetropolitanBank #PakistanCyber #PIIExposure #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Alleged Leak of 12.1 Million Hong Kong Citizen Records Posted on Darkweb  A darkweb forum post claims the release of a massive dataset containing personal information for 12.1 million individuals in Hong Kong. The listing, published on an underground marketplace, alleges that the data was compiled from various sources and includes sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) for a significant portion of the territory's population.  According to the thread, the dataset includes the following fields for each record:  - Name - ID Number - Gender - Birthday - Address - Zip Code - District Details (District 2, 3, and 4) - Mobile Phone Number - Landline Telephone Number - Email Address  The poster provided a link to a sample file hosted on a pastebin service to verify the authenticity of the data. If authentic, the exposure of such granular demographic and contact data could facilitate large-scale phishing campaigns, identity fraud, and targeted social engineering attacks against residents in the region.  Hong Kong has previously experienced significant data breaches, including incidents involving major telecommunications providers and government-related databases, highlighting persistent vulnerabilities in the region's data protection infrastructure. The scale of this alleged leak, covering over 12 million records, would represent one of the largest PII exposures in the area if verified.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by authorities or security researchers.  #DataLeak #HongKong #PII #DarkWeb #IdentityTheft #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🚨Threat Actor Claims Critical 0-Day in NZ Government Certificate API  A threat actor is offering a purported critical zero-day vulnerability for sale on an underground forum, alleging that the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) has exposed its production certificate issuance API to unauthenticated attacks. The post claims the flaw allows attackers to create and modify citizen certificate orders without any form of authentication, potentially compromising the integrity of government records.  According to the listing, the vulnerability affects the DIA's REST API hosted on an Azure API Management gateway. The actor alleges that the endpoint enforces zero authentication, relying solely on a client-version header (X-Version) that can be easily extracted from public JavaScript bundles. The claimed impact includes the ability to submit fake orders with arbitrary Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as names, dates of birth, and birthplaces into the production database.  The seller asserts that the flaw enables several critical actions, including: - Creating fake, persisted certificate orders with arbitrary citizen PII - Modifying existing orders via an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) write without ownership checks - Poisoning data integrity to cause operational disruption or identity fraud - Leaking internal backend infrastructure details via error responses  The Department of Internal Affairs is the primary government agency responsible for maintaining New Zealand's civil records, including births, deaths, marriages, and citizenship. A compromise of this system could have significant implications for national security and public trust in government digital services. The actor has listed the price for the full unredacted Proof of Concept (PoC) at $1,500, demanding payment before revealing the specific URLs, tenant details, and backend hosts.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the New Zealand government or security researchers. The DIA has not yet issued a public statement regarding the claim.  #NewZealand #DIA #ZeroDay #IDOR #AzureAPIM #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity

⚠️ UPDATE: eMUDHRA INTERMEDIATE CA PRIVATE KEYS PROVEN COMPROMISED, NOT JUST WEAK  A new disclosure site for the eMudhra (emSign) incident confirms that the private keys of all eight affected intermediate CAs are compromised. To prove it, the original reporter signed a message with each of the eight private keys and sent the proof to the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs on Oct 17, 2026.  • The eight intermediates chain to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and to Sectigo's cross-signs under Comodo AAA Certificate Services, roots trusted by Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome • Anyone holding one of these keys could impersonate any website or service • Firefox and Chrome have blocked the intermediates since Oct 17, Apple devices since Oct 19, and eMudhra has revoked them • Clients that don't check revocation still trust them until they get an updated CA bundle • Patched: Ubuntu ca-certificates 20260816ubuntu0.x, NSS 3.131.1, Python certifi 2026.10.19, Go 1.27.3 / 1.26.10, curl CA bundle 2026-10-20, rustls-webpki 0.103.16 • Still pending: Debian, Node.js, Bun, FreeBSD  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Our Oct 20 post called these "weak" keys. The issue is bigger than that: the keys are proven compromised, so treat any client that skips revocation checks as exposed. Update CA bundles in OS images, containers, language runtimes and pinned dependencies, then rebuild. On macOS, the built-in /usr/bin/curl checks certificates against /etc/ssl/cert.pem without checking revocation, and that file has not been updated. No fraudulent certificates or active attacks have been reported.  Primary: emudhra.we-have-a-problem[.]com  #DDW #DarkWeb #eMudhra #PKI #TLS #CertificateAuthority #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

NEC published the disclosure on Oct 20, 2026.  What NEC's notice says: • Attackers logged in to customer system environments from the contractor's devices using legitimate accounts • Files on servers were encrypted, leaving various customer systems unusable • Files in a cloud storage space NEC used to share information with customers and the contractor were leaked; they held customers' personal information and system-related information • Affected customers have been contacted individually; NEC has lent the contractor NEC-managed devices and is tightening contractor and personal-data management  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is a compromise of a contractor's access, not an established compromise of NEC's own products or software distribution. NEC has not named the contractor, the affected customers, the number of records or people, or any threat actor, and no ransomware group or ransom demand has been made public, even though files were encrypted. Details of the leaked personal data will be reported to customers as they are confirmed. Organizations that give IT contractors standing access should review those accounts and the shared storage they can reach. 🇯🇵 🚨 YMIRLINK CONFIRMS DATA THEFT FROM ITS CUENOTE FC EMAIL-DELIVERY SERVICE: ~9M RECORDS  Japan's Ymirlink, the company behind the Cuenote email marketing platform, says attackers took personal data out of part of its "Cuenote FC" email-delivery service. Staff spotted the intrusion in the early hours of Oct 16, 2026; Ymirlink first disclosed it on Oct 19 and updated the notice at 19:05 JST the same day.  What Ymirlink's notice says: • The attackers exploited a software flaw, obtained the service login details of Ymirlink support and quality-control staff, planted a malicious program and exported data from databases • They also tried to use those staff credentials to log in to other systems • Five systems on the Cuenote FC dedicated-ASP plan were hit; Ymirlink estimates a cumulative ~9 million records, including email addresses, were exported • Affected servers were cut off from the network, the flaw was patched, the staff credentials were removed from other systems and police were notified; an investigation with outside experts is under way  ⚠️ Analyst Note: ~9 million is a cumulative record count that includes email addresses, not 9 million unique people, and the exact data fields are still being investigated. Five dedicated-plan systems are confirmed affected, not the whole Cuenote service. No threat actor has claimed the attack and no encryption or ransomware has been reported. Cuenote FC sends mail on behalf of businesses, so the exposed addresses likely belong to those businesses' subscribers: Cuenote FC customers should check for a notice from Ymirlink, and recipients should expect phishing that imitates familiar newsletters. 🚨 WEAK eMUDHRA CA KEYS TRIGGER EMERGENCY TRUST UPDATES ACROSS BROWSERS, GO AND PYTHON  The private keys of eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CA certificates were generated so badly that anyone can recover them. A researcher reported it to the Chrome, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft root programs on Oct 17, 2026, Mozilla reproduced the key recovery on its own within hours, and the incident went public on Oct 20.  What the Mozilla incident report shows: • The 8 weak keys are intermediates (6 TLS, 2 code signing) from a single April 2025 key ceremony; they are not eight compromised root CAs • Firefox blocked them via OneCRL and Chrome blocked the 6 TLS keys via CRLSet on Oct 17; eMudhra revoked all 8 on Oct 18 and Sectigo revoked its cross-signs on Oct 19 • Chrome says no TLS certificates chaining to the 6 intermediates were logged to Certificate Transparency before its block; eMudhra says they issued no end-entity certificates • Because several people have now recovered the keys, Mozilla is pulling trust in the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from its root store; Chrome committed to a similar path • eMudhra has stopped issuing under that root and estimates ~30,000 certificates must migrate to its RSA chain  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is flawed key generation, not established key theft, and no active man-in-the-middle campaign has been reported. The risk sits with clients that don't check revocation: until their trust store updates, a certificate signed with these keys could be accepted. Update OS and container trust stores, rebuild Go applications with the patched Go release (CVE-2026-111943, crypto/x509), and upgrade certifi, pip and uv in Python before rebuilding images. Sites on emSign ECC G3 chains should move to new certificates now. The ~30,000 figure counts certificates to replace, not breached systems.  Primary: bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bu… Go fix: github.com/golang/go/issues/… Python guidance: discuss.python.org/t/informa… #DDW #DarkWeb #eMudhra #PKI #TLS #CertificateAuthority #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇰🇼 🚨 KUWAIT: THREAT ACTOR LEAKS ALLEGED CIRCLE DELIVERY APP DATA WITH ~557K CUSTOMER RECORDS  A threat actor on an underground forum has released, for free, data allegedly taken from Circle (trycircle), a Kuwaiti e-commerce and grocery delivery platform.  The actor claims the dataset includes: * About 557,000 customer records (titled as 500K order info) * Customer names and phone numbers * Email addresses * Delivery addresses (area, block, street)  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The sample rows in the listing show Kuwaiti phone numbers and block-and-street delivery addresses, which is enough for targeted delivery scams and WhatsApp or SMS phishing. Because the data was posted for free, anyone can download it, so exposure is wider than in a private sale. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Kuwait #DataBreach #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🇫🇷 🚨 FRANCE: THREAT ACTOR LEAKS ALLEGED ALAIN AFFLELOU E-PRINTING PORTAL DATABASE WITH ~49.7K INVOICE RECORDS  A threat actor on an underground forum has released, for free, a database allegedly taken from an internal e-printing and stationery ordering portal used by Alain Afflelou franchise stores and staff.  The actor claims the dataset includes: * 49,761 lines (about 28 MB) * Invoice numbers, dates and customer codes * Store and franchisee names with billing addresses * Ordered items, quantities, prices and invoice totals  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The listing points to a third-party print-ordering portal rather than Alain Afflelou's core systems, and the sample looks like store-level B2B invoices, not optical or hearing-aid patient records. Sample entries date back to 2015, so part of the data may be old. Franchise contact and billing details can still fuel invoice fraud and phishing against stores. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #France #DataBreach #SupplyChain #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🇹🇼 🚨 TAIWAN: THREAT ACTOR SELLS ALLEGED SENAO DATABASE WITH ~30M RECORDS, INCLUDING PASSWORDS AND HOME ADDRESSES  A threat actor on an underground forum is selling a database allegedly taken from Senao, the Taiwanese mobile phone and electronics retail chain. The listing dates the data to September 2022.  The actor claims the dataset includes: * ~7.42M member accounts with passwords * ~7.39M member records with home addresses * ~7.38M customer table records * ~1.2M orders and ~1.93M order detail lines * ~4.7M mobile device registration records  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If genuine, the mix of account passwords, home addresses and phone registration details would give scammers everything needed for convincing impersonation calls and SMS fraud against Taiwanese consumers. The data is claimed to be from 2022, but reused passwords and unchanged addresses keep old dumps useful. The same seller listed another large Taiwanese e-commerce dataset the same day. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Taiwan #DataBreach #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 OVHCLOUD PULLS SWAPPED CLI RELEASE FILES AFTER A CUSTOMER'S PINNED HASH CAUGHT THE CHANGE  Release files for ovhcloud-cli, OVHcloud's open-source command-line tool, were replaced on GitHub on Oct 19, 2026, weeks after those versions shipped. A customer spotted it when their CI, which pins the SHA-256 of the Linux arm64 archive, started failing.  What the GitHub issue shows: • Five v0.15.0 archives (macOS, Linux, Windows) plus checksums.txt were swapped around 12:47–12:57 UTC; v0.14.0 and v0.13.0 files, including checksums, were also changed by ~13:12 UTC • The reporter found the new "v0.15.0" binary was a local build of a later commit with uncommitted changes, not from the release pipeline; the v0.15.0 tag itself never changed • OVHcloud deleted all affected binaries at 14:21 UTC and shipped v0.16.0 as an immutable release with a signed tag • OVHcloud founder Octave Klaba said the CLI build was compromised by a hacker; a detailed post-mortem is promised  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Pinning the version alone would not have caught this, because the tag and version number stayed the same; the previously pinned hash did. What the swapped binaries did, how many users downloaded them, whether anything was exfiltrated and who was behind it are not confirmed. If you downloaded ovhcloud-cli from GitHub releases on Oct 19 between ~12:47 and 14:21 UTC, delete it, install v0.16.0 and, as a precaution, rotate the OVHcloud API credentials it used. Immutable releases stop files being swapped after publishing; they do not prove a build is clean.  Primary: github.com/ovh/ovhcloud-cli/… Fixed release: github.com/ovh/ovhcloud-cli/… #DDW #DarkWeb #OVHcloud #SupplyChain #GitHub #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇨🇦🇬🇧 🚨 NEW "MIMORI" GROUP CLAIMS OPENTEXT AND AVEVA  A newly surfaced ransomware and extortion group calling itself Mimori has listed two major enterprise software vendors on its leak site: Canada's OpenText and UK-based industrial software maker AVEVA.  The listings carry only generic company descriptions. No data samples, file lists or data volumes have been shown, and these are the first two victims the group has claimed.  The claims have not been independently verified, and neither OpenText nor AVEVA has publicly confirmed an incident.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: OpenText's information-management and security software is used by large enterprises and governments worldwide, and AVEVA's SCADA, HMI and industrial-data platforms run in energy, water, oil and gas and manufacturing sites. A genuine breach at either vendor could carry supply-chain risk for their customers. Brand-new groups often open with high-profile names to build notoriety, so we assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #OpenText #AVEVA #Mimori #Ransomware #Canada #UK #SupplyChain #ICS #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 UPDATE: ZEABUR REPORT SAYS ATTACKER READ 3.2M ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES AND 321K ACCOUNTS  Follow-up to our Oct 16 post. Cloud deployment platform Zeabur has published a preliminary incident report (Oct 19) on the Oct 14–15 breach.  • The attacker used leaked internal credentials (AWS keys and non-expiring cluster admin tokens stored in plaintext) to reach the shared cluster in 9 regions • Root sign-ins to 101 Zeabur-managed GCP Dedicated Servers (92 users) • Confirmed read of the platform database: 3,218,965 service environment-variable records, 321,810 accounts (email, username, phone), 566 plaintext zSend API keys • Commands run in 865 user database services; the attacker mainly hunted for usable API keys, especially AI-service keys • All sessions and platform access tokens revoked; Zeabur says the root cause was its own plaintext long-lived admin credentials  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If you deploy on Zeabur, treat every secret stored there as leaked. Rotate all passwords, database credentials and API keys (especially OpenAI/Anthropic/cloud keys), even if you rotated after the August incident, and watch AI-provider billing for abuse.  Primary: zeabur.com/blogs/october-202… #DDW #DarkWeb #Zeabur #DataBreach #CloudSecurity #APIKeys #SupplyChain #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🇦🇷 🚨 ARGENTINA: TELECOM ARGENTINA'S "PERSONAL" CUSTOMER DATA ALLEGEDLY LEAKED  A threat actor on an underground forum has published a database of about 129,000 records they claim belongs to customers of Personal, the mobile brand of Telecom Argentina.  The actor claims the data includes: * National ID numbers (DNI) and full names * Mobile and landline numbers, service plans * IP addresses, Wi-Fi network names and User-Agent strings * User IDs and server logs  The actor says the data came from a compromised company web service and describes it as recent, covering active customers. The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If authentic, DNI numbers tied to active mobile lines are a ready kit for SIM-swap fraud, account takeover and targeted phishing. Customers should be wary of calls or texts impersonating Personal or their bank. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Telecom Argentina systems were breached.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Argentina #TelecomArgentina #Telecom #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

🇺🇾 🚨 URUGUAY: STATE HEALTH PROVIDER ASSE PATIENT DATABASE ALLEGEDLY LEAKED  A threat actor on an underground forum has leaked what they claim is a database of more than 547,000 records taken from ASSE (Administración de los Servicios de Salud del Estado), Uruguay's main public healthcare provider.  The actor claims the data includes: * Patient names and ID document numbers * Types of medical studies, including COVID-19 testing * Entry dates and billing-related details  The dataset is being shared as a single database file. Patients should be wary of unsolicited calls or messages about test results or bills. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that ASSE systems were breached.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Uruguay #ASSE #Healthcare #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

All of which is to say, it is possible, tho in some other senses unknowable, that if the monarch ever chooses to vote, their right to do so will be in part because they got that right collaterally after joining the EU, and the parliament never subsequently put that unwritten convention to statute

Much later the UK joins the EU, which, among other things, required some of this to all be a lot more explicit. So you later get things like the House of Lords (Reform) Act, where the prohibition on peers voting in elections gets a statutory basis, but the monarch's maybe-incapacity does not

Would the Courts then have prohibited it? Nobody can say. Almost certainly not. But it does mean we can't assume directly that the absence of a statutory prohibition on it means the convention had no weight. That is ~ unknowable
